visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly displays the specified sorted array, indices, target comparison, and binary-search setup, whereas Lesson 1 shows incorrect/garbled array values and misplaced or inconsistent low/high/mid annotations that do not match the given problem.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a well-formed quiz gate with a real question, plausible options, a marked correct answer, and wiring after an existing act, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functional checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has clear, natural narration with spoken math and no raw LaTeX or garbling, while Lesson 1 provides no transcript at all, so its narration quality cannot be verified and is effectively absent.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 includes concrete visual cues timed to the narration references, while Lesson 1 has no transcript or cue data at all, making it unable to demonstrate any synchronization.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly teaches the sorted-array prerequisite, comparison logic, and logarithmic halving argument with mostly accurate values, whereas Lesson 1 has no available transcript or plan to demonstrate any correct or pedagogically useful explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a much more visually polished, consistent neon style with large legible elements, while Lesson 2 is cleaner but feels sparse and unbalanced, with the mid-lesson diagram pushed left, low-contrast text on the right, and visible player UI that detracts from presentation.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: five of six dimension agents preferred it with very high confidence (0.95–0.99), citing correct visuals, functional interactivity, clear narration, synchronized cues, and accurate binary-search instruction.
